node.statement: Every actual row p_i has ||p_i||_1 = 1+2nu(p_i) <= 1+2delta, so any two row points have l1-distance at most 2+4delta. Thus the Lipschitz hypothesis and chi(p_v)=0 give |chi(p_Q)| <= (2+4delta)/s for every fiber Q. For the core C := {Q: |chi(p_Q)| <= L}, grouping coordinates cannot increase variation, so sum_{Q in C}|d_Q| <= sum_Q|d_Q| <= ||q-p_v||_1 = s, and therefore the absolute core contribution is at most Ls.
